title: Organizational Hierarchy Graph
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Organizational Analytics
description: Interactive vis-network tree showing how an organization, its divisions, and its departments are stored as nodes joined by PART_OF edges. Hovering a node highlights its ancestors; clicking a node highlights its descendants.

learningObjectives: Illustrate how organizational hierarchy is represented as a tree of nodes and PART_OF edges in a graph database
prerequisites: Labeled property graph model (nodes, edges, labels, properties)
Basic Cypher MATCH and CREATE patterns

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration of a worked example
keyQuestions: Why do PART_OF edges point from child to parent?
Which node has no outgoing PART_OF edge, and why?
How many hops separate each department from the root?
commonMisconceptions: The hierarchy is a property stored on each node rather than a set of edges
Arrow direction shows who manages whom rather than which unit belongs to which
assessmentOpportunities: Sketch a three-level hierarchy with correctly directed PART_OF edges
Write a Cypher traversal that returns all units beneath a chosen node
